items.title: Fix: clear per-episode visual history in GTBBoxAgent.reset()
items.body:
## Problem

`evaluate_agent()` runs many episodes in a single process, but `GTBBoxAgent.reset()` only clears `rgb_list` (the video frames). The model-input state survives across episodes:

- `self.frame_buffer` (32-frame deque)
- `self._coarse_hist_tokens` (31-frame coarse-token history fed to the planner)
- `self._last_predicted_traj`

So every episode after the first one starts with up to 31 frames of visual history from the **previous episode — usually a different scene and a different target person**. The planner's coarse-history input is corrupted for the first `history` steps of each episode, which hurts early target lock-on (wrong person, wrong direction, early collisions). It also makes results depend on episode ordering / eval chunking.

## Fix

Clear the three buffers in `reset()` (called between episodes by `evaluate_agent`). 10 lines, no behavior change other than starting each episode with a clean history.

## Validation — updated 2026-07-14: full benchmark, all three tasks

**Paired A/B over the full EVT-Bench val protocol** — all **1,380 evaluated episodes per task** (the repo's chunked `get_splits` protocol), on all three tasks. Released checkpoint `omlab/OmTrackVLA-0.6B`; the **only** difference between A and B is this patch (no other changes of any kind). The comparison is episode-matched (same 1,380 episodes on both sides):

| Task | SR ↑ | TR ↑ | CR ↓ | SR flips (fixed-only-win : buggy-only-win) | two-sided sign test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| STT | 71.88 → **78.26** | 78.93 → **81.95** | 9.78 → **4.42** | 126 : 38 | p = 3.2e-12 |
| DT  | 33.99 → **40.29** | 57.76 → **60.78** | 19.35 → **12.32** | 207 : 120 | p = 1.7e-06 |
| AT  | 52.68 → **58.84** | 71.96 → **74.94** | 12.32 → **8.26** | 183 : 98 | p = 4.5e-07 |

Collision flips likewise favor the patch (episodes that *stop* colliding : episodes that *start* colliding): STT **85 : 11**, DT **150 : 53**, AT **87 : 31**.

All nine metrics improve. With the patch, our reproduction also moves substantially closer to the README-reported numbers (STT SR 71.9 → 78.3 vs. 81.41 reported; DT 34.0 → 40.3 vs. 41.54; AT 52.7 → 58.8 vs. 60.04), suggesting that a large share of the commonly-seen reproduction gap on this repo is caused by this cross-episode history contamination.

(Environment: 4×RTX 3090, habitat-sim 0.3.1, transformers 4.57.3, offline local checkpoints. Absolute values can differ slightly across environments, but the A/B comparison above is episode-matched and differs only by this patch. The 230-episode subset results in the original description are superseded by these full-benchmark numbers.)

The fix also makes evaluation results independent of episode ordering / chunking.

items.title: fix(results): push same-repo results to project origin, not a synthesized URL
items.body:
## Problem
For a project whose results live in the same repo (`results.repo_path: .`, `remote: origin`), clicking **Push results** (or auto-push) fails:
```
git push --porcelain origin refs/heads/agentv/results/v1:...
remote: Not Found
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/..git/' not found
```
Even after `git remote set-url origin <correct>`, the push still targets `https://github.com/..git` — AgentV re-derives and rewrites the remote itself.

## Root cause
`resolveResultsRepoUrl()` synthesized a GitHub URL from **any** non-URL string:
`return \`https://github.com/${repo}.git\`` (`packages/core/src/evaluation/results-repo.ts`). With `repo_path: .`, `normalizeResultsConfig` sets `repo = '.'`, so `resolveResultsRepoUrl('.')` → `https://github.com/` + `.` + `.git` = `https://github.com/..git`. That value is then written via `ensureResultsRepoRemote()` (`git remote set-url`), clobbering the correct `origin`.

## Fix (`packages/core/src/evaluation/results-repo.ts`)
- `resolveResultsRepoUrl()` only expands genuine GitHub `owner/repo` shorthand (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/`); explicit URLs pass through; local paths (incl. `.`) are returned unchanged.
- `ensureResultsRepoRemote()` refuses to rewrite an existing remote to a non-URL value, so same-repo results keep using the project's real `origin`. Separate-repo (`repo_url`) behaviour is preserved.

## Validation
- `bun run --filter @agentv/core typecheck` → ✓
- `bun test packages/core/test/evaluation/results-repo.test.ts` → 56 pass, 0 fail (3 new regression tests)

## Summary

The `--backend mock` evaluation harness (documented as the README smoke test) crashed on every condition and produced no results. Two independent defects were responsible; both are fixed here.

## Defects fixed

**1. `MockLLM._generate_response` mis-routed the WBS-draft prompt** (`src/agents/llm_config.py`)
The role-keyword branches (backend / frontend / QA …) were checked *before* the WBS-draft check. Since the WBS-gen prompt body legitimately mentions those roles, the draft request was routed to a review-text response instead of the JSON WBS. WBS parsing then found 0 tasks and the run died with `max() arg is an empty sequence`.
→ Detect the `[WBS Gen Agent]` header first so draft prompts always return the JSON WBS.

**2. `eval_results` import path missing** (`experiments/eval/experiment_runner.py`)
`src/metrics.py` imports `eval_results.autoscore_recompute`, but the runner only put `src/` and the repo root on `sys.path`, so the scoring step raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'eval_results'`.
→ Add `experiments/` to `sys.path` to expose the package.

## Verification

Ran `python ../experiments/eval/experiment_runner.py --backend mock --runs 1` — **26 / 29 conditions now complete** (11 tasks each). The debate-round ablation reproduces the expected monotonic AutoScore curve:

| Condition | rounds | AutoScore |
|-----------|:---:|:---:|
| C0: LLM only | 0 | 0.411 |
| C1: +assignment | 0 | 0.588 |
| C2: +1R debate | 2 | 0.734 |
| C3: +3R debate | 4 | 0.736 |
| C5: +5R debate | 6 | 0.739 |

The remaining 3 failures are the `S2: Frontier` conditions, which require `langchain-google-genai` (gemini backbone) and are unrelated to the mock path.

## Notes

- Running the harness locally also needs team profiles in `sample_data/sample_members/`, which are not tracked in the repo. This PR does **not** add fixture data — it only fixes the code paths.
- The LLM judge reports `N/A` offline (it uses a gemini judge that needs an API key); the deterministic AutoScore/structural metrics are unaffected.
